messages.subject_clean: hypo methylated regions are called as hyper methylated
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr Akalin

I am pretty new to methylkit as well as R. I have tried my best to analyse the problem  and sincere apologies if the problem am facing is because of my lack of experience and knowledge in this field.
I am interested in finding the genes that are differentially methylated (in certain interval on each chromosome) between the wild time and mutant Arabidopsis plants
I have separate files for each interval per chromosome in the required methylkit format. I am trying to analyse one interval at a time.
I have extracted the gene intervals from a gff3 annotation file and converted it into bed format using gff2bed.
I have used this file to define region of interest (genes) by using regionCounts.
if I use it before unite function i get the following message, that i suppose indicated uneven number of observations in my files.

"Error in vecseq(f__, len__, if (allow.cartesian || notjoin) NULL else as.integer(max(nrow(x),  :
  Join results in 1726 rows; more than 1188 = max(nrow(x),nrow(i)). Check for duplicate key values in i, each of which join to the same group in x over and over again. If that's ok, try including `j` and dropping `by` (by-without-by) so that j runs for each group to avoid the large allocation. If you are sure you wish to proceed, rerun with allow.cartesian=TRUE. Otherwise, please search for this error message in the FAQ, Wiki, Stack Overflow and datatable-help for advice."

when I define the regions after unite using the regionCounts followed by calculateDiffMeth and get.methyldiff function, I successfully obtain the DMRs, hypo-methylated regions and hyper-methylated regions. I have exported these lists as bed files and tried to view them using IGV.
I am trying to align the hypo/hyper-methylated regions obtained by methylkit against the  whole genome bisulphite sequencing bedgraph files, I see that the regions that are called hyper methylated are visibly hypo methylated in my mutant as compared to the wildtype. and the regions that are called hypo-methylated are also hypo-methylated.

I am unable to understand why the regions/genes that look hypomethylated are in the list of hypermethylated genes obtained from methylkit. I face the same problem if I do analysis separately on each context (CG, CHH, CHG) or if I do them together.

Many thanks

If you can get a bed12 file from GFF that would be the easiest way to go for you. with your current conversion you are not really getting a bed12 format. bed12 format allows to have exon/intron structure on a single line. You should look it up how a bed12 file looks like and also search this forum on how other users were suggesting to deal with that same problem for the same species.

read.transcript.features() creates a GRangesList object with the following elements
"exons"     "introns"   "promoters" "TSSes"

If you are going to create such a GRangesList object the names should match to the ones above and to get the correct results "exons" GRanges element of the list should only contain exons, "introns" bit should only contain introns, etc.

Best,
Altuna

Hi, answers below

> Do you know which sample number is the maximum to still calculate p values based on the  Fisher's exact test?

This question is not clear but I guess you are referring to number of samples per group to do fisher's exact test. In this case there should be 1 case and 1 control sample at most. If you have more samples per group you can try to use the pool() function to force fisher's exact text. see ?pool

> Additionally, there is this percent methylation, based on which (> 25%), certain bases or regions are called. Can you please give me more information how this number is calculated?

This is the absolute difference between methylation values in test and control when you have 1 case and 1 control

> Is this considering then the average methylation status among the healthy against disease samples?

if you have multiple samples per group, it is the difference between weighted averages by default, see documentation and search the forum for more

> And how is it determined when generating regionwise numbers?

See ?regionCounts and search the forum if documentation is not clear.

> What about minus and plus percentages? Does this indicate hypo and hyper methylated?

Yes, that indicates hyper/hypo status. again search the forum if documentation is not clear, it has been asked many times.
